author: rdc-rfc1-author-c (Claude Haiku 5.5)
rationale: The consumer clock comes from the black-box gate ckgate_hard, whose enable is cleared asynchronously by rst_a_n. Whether a source reset truncates a consumer clock pulse, and how cnt_q releases against that clock, cannot be decided without the cell.

author_reading.rationale: The producer-domain enable feeds a clock gate from an opaque cell whose model is not supplied. Whether the gated clock is held through rst_b_ni release and whether the enable is glitch-free cannot be decided from this RTL.

labels.rationale: cnt_q is clocked by an opaque clock-gating cell output with an unidentified clock, and it is reset by an unconstrained raw rst_b_ni. The gated clock and its enable are not decidable from RTL.
labels.detection_gap: The gated clock is an opaque cell, so RDC-003 can only report its unidentified clock as unresolved.

labels.rationale: A source reset can asynchronously drop the gate enable, but whether that truncates the consumer clock depends on the omitted cell. The consumer reset release timing against that clock is also unspecified.
labels.suspected_flaw: The cell is defined as an empty module without a black-box attribute. Its output is undriven in the literal RTL.

settlement.rationale: Both readers are right on unknown and the generation class. The settler added (* black_box *) to ckgate_hard on line 3, fixing B's flaw. CST-005, RDC-003 (b) and CST-001 disclose the black box and the unidentified clock of the reset register; RDC-002/RDC-011/CDC-002 are incidental.
